Research Portfolio

Interdisciplinary research at the intersection of atmospheric science, climate dynamics, and computational methods. Each project combines rigorous scientific inquiry with innovative analytical approaches.

Research Themes

Atmospheric Chemistry

2 projects

Investigating chemical processes in the atmosphere, particle size distributions, and their impacts on climate and air quality.

Climate Extremes

1 project

Analyzing extreme weather and climate events, their causes, impacts, and future projections using CMIP6 models.

Environmental Data Science

3 projects

Developing computational methods and analytical frameworks for environmental data analysis using R, Python, and MATLAB.

Machine Learning

3 projects

Applying machine learning approaches including Random Forest and GAMs to atmospheric and climate research.

01/2025 - 02/2025
Research Assistant

Applied Generalized Additive Models (GAMs), Mann-Kendall trend tests, and regression analyses in R to identify hydrological and carbon-flux drivers of tree mortality. Research Approach

Methodological Framework

My research combines traditional atmospheric science methods with modern computational approaches, emphasizing reproducibility, transparency, and physical interpretability in all analyses.

Collaborative Approach

I actively seek interdisciplinary collaborations that bring together diverse expertise to address complex environmental challenges from multiple perspectives.
